explanation: Append the root, nonleaf left boundary, all leaves left to right, then the reversed nonleaf right boundary. Excluding leaves from each side boundary and traversing leaves below the root prevents duplicates.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Side walks cost at most O(h), the leaf scan costs O(n), and the right boundary needs reversal storage or recursive frames.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space plus O(b) boundary output space. The leaf traversal and right-boundary reversal/recursion need height-sized auxiliary storage beyond the exterior output.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The exterior separates into four disjoint node groups: the root, nonleaf left boundary, all leaves below the root, and nonleaf right boundary. Following the preferred outward child traces each side boundary. Left-first traversal lists leaves in boundary order, and reversing the right boundary places it bottom-to-top. Excluding leaves from side boundaries and the root from leaf collection prevents repeating nodes, while equal values at different nodes remain valid.
walkthrough: For [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30, null, 4], append root 16, then nonleaf left boundary 7, 2. The leaves are 4, 11, 30. The nonleaf right boundary contributes 25 after reversing its top-down collection. Return [16, 7, 2, 4, 11, 30, 25]. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: A single root is emitted once.
One-sided trees still exclude their leaf from the side-boundary pass.
Deduplication is by which traversal pass owns a node, not by Data value.
